## A decision-first workflow

Use the audit in this order:

1. define the physical change target;
2. verify the full/null model contract;
3. answer Question 1;
4. interpret the source decomposition only within the allowed branch;
5. report numerical and modeling sensitivities.

| Question-1 result | What may be said | What must not be said |
|---|---|---|
| `supported` | “The data support population heterogeneity in the declared slope under this model and bootstrap procedure.” | “Every fitted participant slope is a directly observed change rate.” |
| `unsupported` | “Slope heterogeneity was unsupported by these data.” The decomposition, if returned, is conditional on the fitted positive-variance model. | “There is no heterogeneity.” Do not make individual-slope claims. |
| `numerically_ambiguous` | “The decision is sensitive to unresolved numerical exclusions.” | Any definitive supported/unsupported claim. |
| `indeterminate` | Diagnose the model pair or attempt cap before interpreting. | Treating a failed computation as a scientific result. |

The operational label for every non-supported branch is
**STOP—INDIVIDUAL-SLOPE CLAIM**.

## The three source quantities

`R_direct` is the reliability of the direct within-person slope channel for
the declared estimand. In the balanced independent-residual special case it
coincides with the familiar ordinary least-squares growth-rate reliability.

`D_slope2` is how determinate the fitted random slope is under the full joint
model. It may use the direct slope contrast and other modeled channels.

`Delta_fit = D_slope2 - R_direct` is model-assisted information. It is useful
for diagnosing why a fitted slope appears precise, but it is not another
measurement of observed change.

## Participant and aggregate summaries

The package reports participant-level rows and equal-participant aggregates.
Equal weighting keeps an irregular participant from silently receiving more
scientific weight merely because more rows were retained. Inspect the median,
IQR, minimum, and `has_direct_slope_information`, not only the mean.

A participant with fewer than two usable time points can have
`R_direct = 0` while receiving a model-based slope prediction. Report that as
no direct slope information, not as a precise observed trajectory.

## Residual and covariance assumptions

All quantities are conditional on the declared design and covariance model.
Residual independence, heteroscedasticity, and correlation change the direct
information calculation. The `lmerMod` adapter covers the package's validated
homogeneous independent-residual route. A matrix `R` supplied from elsewhere
supports transparent sensitivity calculations, but does not retroactively
change what `lme4` fitted.

Time recoding does not remove model-assisted information. Under an origin
shift, the random intercept-slope covariance and the centering point transform
together. The relevant covariance with the latent level at the participant's
GLS centering point is invariant.

## Minimum reporting set

Report:

- the six target metadata fields and any `basis_expression`;
- full and null formulas, REML, retained sample, grouping, and residual model;
- observed LR, usable `B`, seed, plus-one p-value, and decision;
- attempt cap, attempts evaluated, target reached, and worst-case decision
  bounds;
- equal-participant means plus distributional summaries of `R_direct`,
  `D_slope2`, and `Delta_fit`;
- counts with no direct slope information and any covariance/rank warning;
- any explicit `B = 4999` escalation or residual-model sensitivity.

## Scope limits

Version 0.1 is a plug-in diagnostic for scalar Gaussian random slopes in the
analysis sample. Parameter-estimation uncertainty is not propagated through
the source decomposition. The package does not yet validate generalized
outcomes, nonlinear change, multivariate targets, external prediction, or a
public participant/bootstrap stability contract.
